title: chore: refactor /spaces module
description:
## Summary

Reorganizes the `spaces` module into per-feature subfolders across all three
layers (`datasources/`, `domain/`, `routes/`). Pure structural refactor — file
moves plus import-path updates, no logic or behavioral changes (148 insertions,
148 deletions, all import paths).

### Subfolders introduced

Each feature area is now self-contained within its layer:

- **address-books** — `datasources/address-books/`, `domain/address-books/`,
  `routes/address-books/` (controllers, services, entities, guards)
- **audit** — `datasources/audit/`, `routes/audit/` (controller, service,
  guard, entities); complements existing `domain/audit/`
- **safes** — `datasources/safes/`, `domain/safes/`, `routes/safes/`
- **spaces** (core) — `datasources/spaces/`, entity moves under `domain/`
- **members** — `routes/members/` (controller, service, `space-invite-email`
  service + template, entities)

### Co-location cleanups

- Test files moved next to their subjects (e.g. `space-assert.utils.spec.ts`
  out of `__tests__/`, audit/address-book dto specs alongside their entities)
- Feature entities, guards, and email templates grouped with their feature

### Import updates

Updated import paths in `spaces.module.ts` and across dependent modules whose
code references the moved files: `counterfactual-safes`, `surveys`, `users`
(member datasource/domain), and `wallets` integration specs.

## Changes

- 87 files changed, 148 insertions(+), 148 deletions(-)
- No production logic changed; DI tokens, controllers, route paths, and
  behavior are unchanged.

## Test plan

- [ ] `yarn test` (unit) passes
- [ ] `yarn test:integration` passes (moved repository integration specs)
- [ ] `yarn test:e2e` passes (moved controller e2e specs)
- [ ] Build / type-check passes (verifies all import paths resolve)

findings.claim: This file was moved and edited but is missing the required '// SPDX-License-Identifier: FSL-1.1-MIT' header that project convention requires on every created or modified file.
The commit message for 976f1ed contains a typo, reading 'chore: sl=plit into domain subfolders' instead of the intended wording.

The CI license-check step builds its file list with 'git diff --name-only --diff-filter=AM', which excludes files git reports as renames; since the moved DTO files are detected as renames, CI will not flag their missing license headers.
The guide states that feature DB entities live under datasources/entities/, but spaces now uses datasources/<subdomain>/entities/, so the documented placement rule is out of date for this module.
The guide still calls src/modules/spaces the large product-module example to copy without describing its new per-subdomain shape, so it no longer accurately represents the module's structure.

Domain-layer code imports 'InviteUserInput' from the routes layer ('spaces/routes/members/entities/'), which violates the layering order defined in AGENTS.md; this pre-existing issue is now more visible after the file move.

The new spaces/ subfolder convention is applied only in the datasources layer, while the domain and routes layers keep spaces-core files mixed at the top level alongside feature subfolders, creating an inconsistent structure across the three layers.

The CI license-check step's use of '--diff-filter=AM' means it never checks renamed files for license headers; changing the filter to 'AMR' would close this gap, though the fix is outside the scope of this diff.

Domain-layer code imports 'InviteUserInput' from the routes layer ('spaces/routes/members/entities/'), which violates the layering order defined in AGENTS.md; this pre-existing issue is now more visible after the file move.
Domain-layer code imports 'UpsertAddressBookItemsDto' from the routes layer, violating the layering order defined in AGENTS.md; this pre-existing issue is now more visible after the file move.

The glob src/modules/spaces/routes/*service.ts now only matches spaces.service.ts because the other route services moved into routes/{address-books,audit,members,safes}/, making the documented glob misleading.

The core Space DB entity was placed in a spaces/ subfolder under datasources/, while the corresponding core files in domain/ (domain/spaces.repository.ts, domain/entities/space.entity.ts) and routes/ (routes/spaces.controller.ts) remain at the layer root, creating an inconsistent subdomain layout across layers; either the core entity should stay at the root of datasources/ or the spaces/ subfolder should be added consistently in all three layers.
This moved file does not start with the required SPDX license header, so the license-headers CI job that runs insert-license on changed files should fail.
This moved file does not start with the required SPDX license header, so the license-headers CI job that runs insert-license on changed files should fail.
This file was moved and edited but is missing the required '// SPDX-License-Identifier: FSL-1.1-MIT' header that project convention requires on every created or modified file.
The commit message in 976f1ed contains a typo ("sl=plit" instead of "split") that should be corrected on squash-merge.
Domain-layer code imports 'UpsertAddressBookItemsDto' from the routes layer, violating the layering order defined in AGENTS.md; this pre-existing issue is now more visible after the file move.

The "Copy" list still names src/modules/spaces/routes/entities/address-book-request.dto.entity.ts, but that file has moved to src/modules/spaces/routes/address-books/entities/address-book-request.dto.entity.ts, so the documentation no longer matches the actual file layout.

Code for the 'spaces' area is now split across three different organizational patterns depending on layer: datasources code sits in a new 'datasources/spaces/' subfolder, while domain and routes code remain at their layer root, making it unclear where a new spaces-related file should be placed going forward.
The file defines a single entity class SpaceSafe but the filename is plural, which is inconsistent naming; this is pre-existing but the refactor was an opportunity to fix it.

Spaces-core files in the domain layer are not grouped into a spaces/ subfolder even though the datasources layer now uses this convention, so a reader has to learn that files without a subfolder belong to the spaces feature.

Spaces-core files in the routes layer (controller, service, DTO entities, guard) are not grouped into a spaces/ subfolder, leaving the same inconsistency as in the domain layer relative to datasources.
